core.p: Oxygen is produced at the **anode** (positive electrode) when solutions such as **dilute sulfuric acid** or **sodium sulfate solution** are electrolysed with inert electrodes. Hydroxide ions are discharged and oxygen gas bubbles off. The glowing splint test confirms the gas is oxygen.
bullets: Anode half equation (HT): 4OH- → O2 + 2H2O + 4e-
Hydroxide ions lose electrons, so this is oxidation
Hydrogen is formed at the cathode: 2H+ + 2e- → H2
Volume of hydrogen is twice the volume of oxygen when water is electrolysed

callouts.p: If a question asks how to show the anode gas is oxygen, answer 'glowing splint relights'.

core.p: Plants and algae release oxygen during **photosynthesis**: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2. Gas bubbles given off by pondweed in light can be collected and shown to be oxygen with a glowing splint. This links to how oxygen built up in Earth's atmosphere.
bullets: Collect the bubbles in an upturned test tube over the pondweed
Enough gas must collect for the test to work
A relighting splint shows the gas is rich in oxygen

core.h: Why air does not relight the splint
core.p: Air contains oxygen, yet the glowing splint does not relight in air. This is because the oxygen is **diluted** by nitrogen (about 78%). The test therefore really shows a **high concentration of oxygen**, not just the presence of a little oxygen.
bullets: Air: about 21% oxygen, so the splint just keeps glowing
Gas mixtures with a high percentage of oxygen relight the splint
If the test tube contains a lot of air, the test may fail even when some oxygen is present

callouts.p: The splint relights because the concentration of oxygen is much higher than in air.

core.p: Practical errors can give a false negative, where oxygen is present but the splint does not relight.
bullets: Testing too slowly lets oxygen escape and air mix in
The splint has stopped glowing before it is inserted
The splint touches water in the tube and goes out
Too little gas collected
Fix: collect a full tube, stopper it, use a strongly glowing splint and test immediately

core.p: Gas test questions are usually 2 marks: **one mark for the test** and **one for the result**. Both must be precise.
bullets: Mark 1: 'insert a glowing splint'
Mark 2: 'it relights'
Do not describe a lit splint, a pop, or limewater for oxygen
If asked to 'identify the gas', give the test and the result and name the gas

callouts.p: Test + result. 'Glowing splint relights' gets both marks in four words.

analogy.t: A dying campfire and a bellows
analogy.p: A glowing splint is like a campfire that has died down to embers. Blowing air onto embers with a bellows can make them flare up, and pure oxygen is like an extremely powerful bellows: so many oxygen molecules arrive that the embers burst back into flame. The analogy breaks down because a bellows works mainly by delivering more air faster, whereas in the test the oxygen is not moving; it is the much higher concentration of oxygen molecules, not a draught, that speeds up the reaction.

terms.d: A wooden splint that has been lit and blown out, so only the tip glows red.
Bursts back into flame; the positive result for oxygen.
Allows other substances to burn; oxygen supports combustion but is not itself a fuel.
An exothermic reaction in which a substance reacts with oxygen, releasing heat and light.
The amount of a substance in a given volume; pure oxygen has a much higher oxygen concentration than air.
A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up, e.g. manganese(IV) oxide.
H2O2; decomposes into water and oxygen: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2.
MnO2, a black solid used as a catalyst for decomposing hydrogen peroxide.
A reaction in which one substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
Collecting a gas by letting it displace water from an upturned tube; suits gases that are not very soluble.
The positive electrode in electrolysis, where oxygen may be produced.
The positive result for hydrogen with a lighted splint.
Calcium hydroxide solution; turns milky with carbon dioxide.
Colour removed; damp litmus paper is bleached white by chlorine.

mistakes.w: Put a lit splint in the gas: it squeaky pops.
mistakes.r: That is the hydrogen test. For oxygen, a glowing splint relights.

mistakes.w: The splint burns brighter.
mistakes.r: The glowing splint relights.

mistakes.w: Oxygen burns.
mistakes.r: Oxygen supports combustion; it is not a fuel.

mistakes.w: Oxygen turns limewater milky.
mistakes.r: Limewater tests for carbon dioxide.

mistakes.w: Put a glowing splint in the gas: it goes out, so it is oxygen.
mistakes.r: A glowing splint RELIGHTS in oxygen; going out suggests oxygen is not present in high concentration.

mistakes.w: The splint relights because oxygen is hot.
mistakes.r: The higher concentration of oxygen increases the rate of combustion.

mistakes.w: Manganese(IV) oxide reacts to make oxygen.
mistakes.r: It is a catalyst; hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2.

mistakes.w: Air relights a glowing splint because it contains oxygen.
mistakes.r: Air is only about 21% oxygen, so the splint does not relight.

exam.q: Describe the test for oxygen.
model: Insert a glowing splint
It relights
exam.tip: Test and result, one mark each.

exam.q: Name the gas that relights a glowing splint.
model: Oxygen
exam.tip: Not 'air'.

exam.q: Explain why a glowing splint relights in oxygen but not in air.
model: Pure oxygen has a higher concentration of oxygen than air (about 21%)
So combustion is faster / more frequent collisions, enough to make the splint burst into flame
exam.tip: Use the idea of concentration.

exam.q: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes to form water and oxygen. Write the balanced equation.
model: Correct formulae (1), balanced (1)
exam.tip: Check O atoms: 4 on each side.

exam.q: State the role of manganese(IV) oxide in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.
model: Catalyst (speeds up the reaction without being used up)
exam.tip: One word is enough.

exam.q: A student tests a gas with a lighted splint and hears a squeaky pop. Name the gas.
model: Hydrogen
exam.tip: Lit splint = hydrogen.

exam.q: Give the test and result for carbon dioxide and for oxygen.
model: Carbon dioxide: bubble through limewater
Limewater turns milky / cloudy
Oxygen: insert a glowing splint
Splint relights
exam.tip: Keep each test paired with its own result.

exam.q: During electrolysis of sodium sulfate solution a gas forms at the anode. Describe how you could show it is oxygen.
model: Collect the gas and insert a glowing splint
It relights
exam.tip: Same test wherever the gas comes from.

exam.q: Suggest why a student's glowing splint did not relight even though the tube contained some oxygen.
model: Too much air in the tube / oxygen escaped because the test was too slow
So the oxygen concentration was too low (or the splint was no longer glowing)
exam.tip: Think about concentration and technique.

exam.q: Describe how you could prepare a test tube of oxygen and show that it is oxygen. (6 marks)
model: Add hydrogen peroxide to a flask containing manganese(IV) oxide
Manganese(IV) oxide acts as a catalyst: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2
Connect a delivery tube to an upturned test tube full of water in a trough
Discard the first tube of gas (air); collect oxygen as it displaces the water
Stopper the tube under water
Insert a glowing splint: it relights, showing oxygen
exam.tip: Method in order, then test and result.

worked.q: Four test tubes contain oxygen, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and air. Describe how to identify the tube of oxygen.
steps: Insert a glowing splint into each tube in turn
In air the splint keeps glowing (only about 21% oxygen)
In carbon dioxide the splint goes out
In hydrogen the glowing splint may give a pop as hydrogen ignites
In oxygen the glowing splint relights
worked.ans: The tube in which the glowing splint relights contains oxygen.

worked.q: Model answer (3 marks): Explain, using collision theory, why a glowing splint relights in oxygen.
steps: Pure oxygen has a much higher concentration of oxygen molecules than air
So oxygen molecules collide with the hot wood more frequently, giving more successful collisions per second
The rate of combustion increases and releases heat fast enough for the splint to burst into flame
worked.ans: Higher oxygen concentration → more frequent collisions → faster combustion → splint relights.

worked.q: Applied example: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2. How many molecules of oxygen form from 10 molecules of hydrogen peroxide?
steps: Ratio of H2O2 to O2 is 2 : 1
worked.ans: 5 molecules of oxygen.
